name: v6-f-breadth
note: V6 iteration 4. Evidence on the development tasks: D (curriculum v1 = 76 families, 4 write + 2 bug-fix examples each, full budget, half legacy) is the best candidate (all_clean 30 vs 29) and learns its families well (new family members: code loss 1.32 -> 0.45), but transfer to unseen-v1 plateaued (C 0.739 -> D 0.676 -> E 0.672): more depth on the same families no longer helps. E's additions (plausible-but-wrong repairs, worked examples) cost 4 dev bug fixes (whole-body rewrites taught rewriting instead of minimal edits) without more transfer. Changed variable vs D: breadth - the same curriculum budget spread over curriculum v3 (215 families: v1 + 19 algorithm families + 120 families written without reading any evaluation set), 1 write + 1 bug-fix example each (~133k curriculum tokens, about D's 129k: v3 programs are longer), D's answer formats only (no repairs, no worked examples). Recipe, legacy share and evaluation as D.
decision: Same pre-registered rule as v6-c-idioms: replaces round 54 only if every seed beats its all_clean (29/168), the mean gain is >= 3 items, and no category loses >= 3 clean items round 54 passes. unseen-v2 is the fixed holdout: never trained on, never used to choose between experiments. The benchmark is reported only.
